label: Частый / Редкий
description: Частый vs редкий: frequent/rare contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Частый' takes the masculine ending to match 'снег'. The weather note anchors the form in a common seasonal observation.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Редкая' takes the feminine ending to match 'фамилия'. The everyday remark roots the feminine form in daily speech.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Редкое' takes the neuter ending to match 'явление'. The phrase fixes the neuter form in a concrete observation.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Частые' takes the plural ending to match 'боли'. The familiar complaint anchors the plural form.
Strategic focus: Direct plural contrast. 'Частые' is plural nominative for 'гости' while 'редкими' is plural instrumental after 'стали'. The sentence pairs both adjectives in one shift.
Strategic focus: Plural predicate adjective. 'Редкие' follows the noun as a predicate describing 'дожди'. The everyday weather remark grounds the form.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'были', 'редкими' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'визиты'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Masculine nominative in a sentence. 'Редкий' takes the masculine ending to match 'цветок'. The nature scene makes the masculine form concrete.
Strategic focus: Short-form plural predicate. The short form 'редки' states a present quality of the subject 'случаи'. Short forms are typical when stating a general truth.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Реже' is the comparative of 'редкий' and stays the same for any gender. The sentence compares the present frequency to the past.
